analysis:
Both units are head-side text of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1427-1782), which is release-note prose describing v0.10.9 and earlier behavior. The patch excerpt shows the PR only adds a v0.10.13 candidate section (lines 11-45); the supplied units are unchanged historical changelog text surrounding it. No executable code, configuration or trust-boundary logic is modified in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant claims examined for consistency with the threat model: (1) Xcode 27.2 weak-import Date comparison availability fix, which matches the header note on A-018 availability. (2) `darkbloom cluster gpu-limit`, which is consistent with TB-014/A-020/T-062: owner confirmation plus a macOS administrator prompt, never changed automatically, and read-back verification. (3) Sandbox setup `--disk` option passing drives to the add-on installer, relevant to TB-013/T-061; the changelog gives no evidence of a regression in installer integrity checks. (4) Single-Mac serving stepping aside and `stop --solo`, which relate to local lifecycle control; no new authorization boundary is visible. (5) The registration is stated unchanged, with MLX pins unchanged. (6) The known limitation that DevNet and production apps on the same Mac can read each other's pair state and that `--forget` can remove production's login job is a disclosed local availability and integrity limitation affecting only dual-install Macs. It is documented, not newly introduced by this diff, and the evidence does not show a code change.

A changelog is documentation and cannot itself create a regression. Remaining questions for integration are whether the actual code for the v0.10.13 loop guard (`DARKBLOOM_LOOP_EXIT_THINKING`) and the joining-Mac stop handling is in other batches. Those are outside the supplied units, so I am making no claims about them.
